newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya to hold public inquest on student death.
newsitem.headline: Kenya to hold public inquest on student death.

text.p: Kenya's Attorney General announced on Wednesday a public inquest into the death of student leader Solomon Muruli who died in suspicious circumstances last month, sparking student protests.

Muruli, a 23-year-old University of Nairobi student, was burnt to death in a blaze in his room on campus on February 23. Two universities were closed after violent protests from students who accused police of murdering him.
"The public inquest will go into all the circumstances surrounding the suspicious death of Mr Solomon Muruli," said a statement by Attorney General Amos Wako.
The inquest would also look into events leading up to Muruli's death, the statement said.
Muruli said plain clothes police officers abducted and interrogated him over a period of four days in November before he was dumped in the grounds of a church at Kiambu, near Nairobi, on December 3.
He was arrested in January and released without charge and claimed to have received a series of death threats.
The inquest falls short of demands by opposition members of parliament who wanted British police to investigate and human rights groups who called for a judicial commission of inquiry.
Assistant deputy public prosecutor Justus Bwonwonga was named head of the inquest, which follows a police investigation into the death.

President Daniel arap Moi who faces elections this year sacked the police commissioner last December after police shot dead two students at Nairobi's Kenyatta University and one student at Egerton University.
Kenya students have no clear political agenda, at least in public, and usually only protest about fees and conditions.
